rounds.proof_sketch: Grid launched with dim3(batch_size) where batch_size=128. Thus blockIdx.x ∈ [0,127]. Original guard: batch_idx >= 128 → always false. Mutated guard: batch_idx >= 129 → always false. Both predicates evaluate identically for all reachable block indices.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the early-return boundary check from `batch_idx >= batch_size` to `batch_idx >= batch_size + 1`. With fixed input shape [128, 4096], batch_size=128 and the kernel is launched with exactly 128 blocks (grid dimension = batch_size). Since blockIdx.x can only take values 0 through 127, neither the original condition (batch_idx >= 128) nor the mutated condition (batch_idx >= 129) can ever be true. Both conditions always evaluate to false, meaning no thread ever takes the early-return path in either version. The guard is protective dead code that only matters if the grid were launched with more blocks than batch elements, which never happens under this kernel's launch configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation affects a boundary guard that is never triggered because the grid dimension exactly matches batch_size. To kill this mutant would require launching more blocks than batch elements, which requires changing the kernel launch parameters or batch size, neither of which is permitted.
rounds.recommendations: When testing boundary guard mutations in CUDA kernels, check whether the guard condition is ever reachable given the kernel's launch configuration. Guards of the form `if (idx >= N) return` where grid dimension equals N are dead code and mutations to them are equivalent. Consider documenting or removing such guards if they can never be triggered, or restructuring the launch to make the guard meaningful.
